Eight links, each checked this session and confirmed to load.

- **[ICH Q9(R1), Quality Risk Management](https://database.ich.org/sites/default/files/ICH_Q9%28R1%29_Guideline_Step4_2023_0126_0.pdf)**
  (PDF, ICH, final version adopted 18 January 2023). The actual guideline this module is built
  on: Section 4 gives the Risk Assessment → Risk Control → Risk Communication → Risk Review
  lifecycle in full, Section 5 covers formality, risk-based decision-making, and managing
  subjectivity (the R1-specific additions), and Annex I describes FMEA, Risk Ranking and
  Filtering, and the other named tools. Read this when you want the source itself, not this
  lesson's paraphrase of it. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[21 CFR 606.100, Standard operating procedures — Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/606.100)**
  Free, reliably reachable mirror of the regulatory floor this module reuses — paragraph (c)'s
  "thorough investigation... conclusions and followup" requirement, which underlies any
  risk-based investigation depth regardless of how formal the process. Use this when you need
  the regulation's own wording quickly, without going through eCFR's blocked rendered pages.
  Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Title 21 — Code of Federal Regulations — GovInfo](https://www.govinfo.gov/app/collection/cfr/2024/title21)**
  The U.S. Government Publishing Office's official CFR collection, one level up from a single
  section. Use this as a fallback source, or to browse Part 606 and its neighboring parts
  directly, when you need to confirm a citation against the government's own publication rather
  than a secondary mirror. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[ICH Q9(R1): Quality Risk Management​](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6twBwRyAZf4)**
  (BioBoston Consulting, from oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this lesson. A
  pharma-consulting educational channel walking through ICH Q9(R1) directly — the exact guideline
  revision this module is built on. It's general pharma-industry framing, not blood-specific, and
  it won't mention Lakeshore or tracked distribution — watch it for the four-stage lifecycle and
  the R1 formality point, then map both onto this lesson's own FMEA. Verified embeddable via
  YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[iSixSigma: FMEA — Failure Mode and Effects Analysis](https://www.isixsigma.com/tools-templates/fmea/)**
  — a widely used Six Sigma / quality-engineering explainer of FMEA specifically: how to name
  failure modes, score severity/occurrence/detection, and compute a risk priority number (RPN).
  Distinct from the general likelihood/severity/detectability vocabulary `risk-and-controls-
  vocabulary` already covered — use this when you want FMEA's own mechanics argued in full,
  outside this lesson's one worked table. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Pharmaceutical Technology: A New Risk-based GMP Inspection Planning Tool](https://www.pharmtech.com/view/new-risk-based-gmp-inspection-planning-tool)**
  — covers the PIC/S (Pharmaceutical Inspection Co-operation Scheme) risk-based inspection
  planning model, built directly on ICH Q9's QRM framework, which ranks manufacturing sites by
  risk to decide which get inspected first. A real-world case of risk ranking and filtering doing
  exactly the job this lesson's own example does — deciding which satellite site to audit first —
  just at regulator scale instead of Lakeshore's. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP
  200).

- **[Greenlight Guru: ISO 14971 Medical Device Risk Management: What to Know](https://www.greenlight.guru/blog/iso-14971-medical-device-risk-management)**
  — an explainer on ISO 14971, the international standard for risk management across a medical
  device's lifecycle (plan, analyze, evaluate, control, monitor). Not itself cited anywhere in
  this lesson, but worth knowing as the standard most often compared to ICH Q9: both run a
  near-identical assess-control-review lifecycle, from the medical-device side of the same
  regulatory family rather than the pharma/biologics side. Verified loading via `curl` on
  2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[InvGate: ITIL & Risk Management: How Do They Relate?](https://blog.invgate.com/itil-4-best-practice-overviews-risk-management)**
  — an ITSM-angle explainer of ITIL 4's Risk Management general management practice and the risk
  register as its central tool. Backs this module's own ITIL bridge — a risk register with a
  named lifecycle (assess, control, communicate, review) instead of a spreadsheet updated when
  someone remembers — argued in full ITIL terms before mapping it onto ICH Q9(R1)'s own four
  stages. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

## Keep learning

Not official sources — good places to learn more about quality risk management and FMEA.

- **[ICH Q9 Quality Risk Management](https://www.gmp-compliance.org/guidelines/gmp-guideline/ich-q9-quality-risk-management)** (ECA Academy) — A commentary-style hub on the guideline and its revision, useful as a second explanation next to the primary text. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[Failure mode and effects analysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Failure_mode_and_effects_analysis)** (Wikipedia) — Clear overview of severity, occurrence and detection scoring and the risk priority number, with worked tables. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[Risk management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Risk_management)** (Wikipedia) — General background on identifying, assessing and treating risk across industries; also underlies CISSP Domain 1 (Security and Risk Management) thinking. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
